# Fork-maintained patches for rayward-external/bifrost
#
# These are CodeQL false-positive suppressions on operator-configured log lines.
# Upstream (maximhq/bifrost) does not carry inline CodeQL annotations.
# If upstream rewrites these plugin files, the suppressions may be lost.
#
# Format: <file> | <grep_pattern_that_proves_patch_is_present> | <human_description>

transports/Dockerfile.custom               | golang:1.26.4                 | build fix: builder image Go must be >= the version in core/go.mod (GOTOOLCHAIN=local won't auto-upgrade); bump in step with go.work on every upstream sync or the image build fails at `go work init`
.github/workflows/snyk.yml                 | astral-sh/setup-uv            | infra fix: use astral-sh/setup-uv, NOT step-security/setup-uv (the latter hard-fails private-repo CI with "Subscription is not valid"); upstream/-X theirs syncs keep reverting this
.github/workflows/release-cli.yml          | DISABLED via `gh workflow disable` (state in GitHub Actions, NOT the file) | infra fix: upstream-only release — publishes maxim's standalone cli/ tool to UPSTREAM's R2 bucket + pushes cli/vX tags. Fork has no GH_TOKEN/R2_* secrets, so the release-cli job's checkout fails on EVERY push to main ("Input required and not supplied: token"). Has no purpose on the fork. Disabled via gh (disabled_manually) so it stops firing; the file stays vanilla. Verify with `gh workflow view "Release CLI" --repo rayward-external/bifrost` (state should be disabled_manually). REMOVAL CONDITION: re-enable only if the fork ever needs to ship its own CLI build with its own secrets.
.github/workflows/npx-publish.yml          | DISABLED via `gh workflow disable` (state in GitHub Actions, NOT the file) | infra fix: upstream-only release — publishes @maximhq/bifrost-cli to UPSTREAM's npm. Same failure class as release-cli (checkout token not supplied); fires on cli/ version bumps. No purpose on the fork. Disabled via gh (disabled_manually). REMOVAL CONDITION: re-enable only if the fork ever publishes its own npm package with its own NPM_TOKEN.
.github/workflows/pr-test-notifier.yml     | DISABLED via `gh workflow disable` (state in GitHub Actions, NOT the file) | infra fix: upstream bug — workflow triggers `on: push: branches: [main]` but its only step runs `gh pr comment ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} --repo ... --body ...`; on a push event pull_request.number is empty, so gh errors "argument required when using the --repo flag" and the "Post Test Instructions" job fails on EVERY push to main. Posting a "test this PR" comment is meaningless on push-to-main (no PR). Cannot fix the trigger in-file (token lacks `workflow` scope). Disabled via gh (disabled_manually) like release-cli/npx-publish. Verify with `gh workflow view "PR Test Notifier" --repo rayward-external/bifrost` (state should be disabled_manually). REMOVAL CONDITION: re-enable if upstream changes the trigger to `pull_request` (then it would have a real PR number) or the fork ever wants PR test-instruction comments.

Dismiss step passes dismissals through an env var (not interpolated into the `echo '...'` string) because the required dismissed_reason value "won't fix" contains an apostrophe that breaks single-quoted shell interpolation of `${{ inputs.dismissals }}` (run #28735975130 failed with exit 127); env-var indirection avoids the quoting break and is standard hygiene against script injection from untrusted expression values.

transports/bifrost-http/server/server.go            | RegisterKnownProvider      | bug fix: ReloadProvider did not call schemas.RegisterKnownProvider for custom providers, so ParseModelString could not split "provider/model" strings until the first request triggered prepareProvider internally; the very next chat request after POST /api/providers routed to a wildcard-keyed standard provider (HuggingFace), failed, and logged status="error" under the original request-id — causing assertLoggingTrace() in run-observability-local.mjs to fail; fix: call schemas.RegisterKnownProvider(provider) in ReloadProvider when providerInfo.CustomProviderConfig != nil; idempotent for standard providers; REMOVAL CONDITION: remove when upstream adds equivalent call in its own ReloadProvider
tests/e2e/api/runners/run-observability-local.mjs   | model.*modelName           | test fix (companion to ReloadProvider RegisterKnownProvider fix): with correct provider/model split the OTEL model attribute and Prometheus model label are modelName ("hello-world"), not requestedModel ("provider/hello-world"); upstream test checks requestedModel as the exact metric label — correct for unregistered providers but wrong after the routing fix; change the two strict assertions (OTEL metrics binary check and Prometheus label map) to use modelName; Prometheus polling (line 296-297) already accepts both; REMOVAL CONDITION: remove when upstream either registers known providers in ReloadProvider or changes these assertions to accept modelName

framework/vectorstore/redis.go                      | index already exists       | bug fix: CreateNamespace's FT.INFO existence check and FT.CREATE are not atomic, so concurrent callers (the semanticcache suite fans out one Plugin.Init per vector store under t.Parallel) both observe "not exists" and race to FT.CREATE; the loser failed test-plugins with "failed to create semantic vector index BifrostSemanticCachePluginTest: Index already exists". Fix: treat the benign "Index already exists" FT.CREATE error as the idempotent success the FT.INFO-hit path already returns. Guarded by TestRedisStore_CreateNamespace_ConcurrentIsIdempotent. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove when upstream makes Redis CreateNamespace tolerate the racing-create case

# 2026-06-18: fixed assertLoggingTrace() failure in test-api-integrations (branch fix/post-sync-137-followup): ReloadProvider in server.go did not call RegisterKnownProvider, so the custom provider name was unknown to ParseModelString at request time → request routed to HuggingFace (wildcard key) → failed → logged status="error" under original request-id; companion test patch changes OTEL-metrics and Prometheus strict label assertions in run-observability-local.mjs from requestedModel to modelName (correct after split routing). plugins/logging go test passes; local observability check prints "passed".
# 2026-06-18: fixed test-plugins semanticcache flake (branch fix/redis-createnamespace-race): TestSemanticCache_AllVectorStores_ParameterFiltering/Redis intermittently failed with "Index already exists" — a TOCTOU race in framework/vectorstore/redis.go CreateNamespace (FT.INFO check then FT.CREATE not atomic; parallel Plugin.Init calls both create the shared BifrostSemanticCachePluginTest index). Fix treats the benign FT.CREATE "Index already exists" error as idempotent success; added TestRedisStore_CreateNamespace_ConcurrentIsIdempotent regression (fails without the fix, passes with). No workflow files changed.
# 2026-06-19: disabled PR Test Notifier via `gh workflow disable` — upstream bug: it triggers on push to main but its only step runs `gh pr comment ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}`, which is empty on a push event → "argument required when using the --repo flag", failing the Post Test Instructions job on every push to main. Meaningless on push-to-main (no PR). Can't fix trigger in-file (no workflow scope); disabled via gh like release-cli/npx-publish. State-only change; file stays vanilla.
# 2026-07-06: security sweep — code-scanning alerts: 0 open (verified via alert-bridge.yml list run). Dependency vulns: 0 across go (govulncheck -scan=module against an offline mirror of golang/vulndb, all 39 go.mod modules — vuln.go.dev and api.osv.dev are both blocked by this session's egress policy, see PR for detail), npm (npm audit, all 11 package.json dirs with dependencies), python/uv (pip-audit --strict, tests/integrations/python), and cargo (cargo audit, examples/plugins/hello-world-wasm-rust). Fixed .github/dependabot.yml: removed a stale entry pointing at nonexistent /plugins/litellmcompat (the real directory is /plugins/compat, already covered by its own entry) and added a missing `uv` ecosystem entry for /tests/integrations/python so Dependabot covers every ecosystem in the repo.
